messages.text: Rybakina too strong for Osaka as Zheng stuns Swiatek at US Open

metadata.summary: Elena Rybakina cruised into the US Open quarter-finals with a straight-sets victory over Naomi Osaka to keep her push for the world No 1 ranking on track.
metadata.content: US Open 2026: Elena Rybakina too strong for Naomi Osaka as Qinwen Zheng comeback stuns Iga Swiatek | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to content US Open 2026: Elena Rybakina too strong for Naomi Osaka as Qinwen Zheng comeback stuns Iga Swiatek Elena Rybakina beats Naomi Osaka in 66 minutes to set up a quarter-final against Qinwen Zheng, who mounted a stunning comeback to beat Iga Swiatek; Mirra Andreeva also into last eight with win over Anastasia Potapova; watch the US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis Monday 7 September 2026 23:25, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Naomi Osaka's match against Elena Rybakina at the US Open. Elena Rybakina cruised into the US Open quarter-finals with a straight-sets victory over Naomi Osaka to keep her push for the world No 1 ranking on track. Rybakina will reclaim the top spot if she reaches the semi-finals, and after dismantling two-time champion Osaka on Louis Armstrong, she has every reason to believe she can go all the way and lift the US Open trophy. It took the second seed just over 20 minutes to wrap up the first set 6-1 before securing a decisive break midway through the second to quell a resurgent Osaka and seal an emphatic 6-1 6-4 victory. metadata.summary: Oleksandr Usyk's manager has dismissed Tyson Fury's call for a third fight with the Ukrainian amid continued doubt over an all-British heavyweight showdown with Anthony Joshua.
metadata.content: Oleksandr Usyk's manager dismisses Tyson Fury's offer to be 'backup plan' for Anthony Joshua fight amid doubt over heavyweight clash | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to content Oleksandr Usyk's manager dismisses Tyson Fury's offer to be 'backup plan' for Anthony Joshua fight amid doubt over heavyweight clash A long-awaited heavyweight fight between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua has been stuck in negotiations in recent months amid an apparent disagreement over the location for the proposed clash in November; Fury called out Oleksandr Usyk on Monday Monday 7 September 2026 21:26, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tyson Fury calls out Oleksandr Usyk in a social media video after claiming Anthony Joshua will never fight the Gypsy King Oleksandr Usyk's manager has dismissed Tyson Fury's call for a third fight with the Ukrainian amid continued doubt over an all-British heavyweight showdown with Anthony Joshua. With protracted negotiations over a long-awaited Fury-Joshua bout being held up by a dispute over where the fight would take place, Fury took to social media on Monday to say he was looking for a new opponent. Fury said he wants a third fight with Usyk, who became undisputed heavyweight champion as he beat Fury twice on points in 2024. metadata.content: Isack Hadjar to miss Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid due to wrist injury as Liam Lawson continues at Red Bull | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Isack Hadjar to miss Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid due to wrist injury as Liam Lawson continues at Red Bull Red Bull confirm Isack Hadjar will miss a third straight race due to his ongoing wrist injury; Liam Lawson replaces him as Max Verstappen's team-mate again; watch every session of the Spanish Grand Prix at a new track in Madrid from this Friday, live on Sky Sports F1 Nigel Chiu Sports Journalist @NigelCJourno Tuesday 8 September 2026 01:11, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Craig Slater reveals further details about Isack Hadjar's injury ahead of the Dutch GP. Isack Hadjar will miss this weekend's Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid as he continues to recover from a fractured wrist. Liam Lawson will replace Hadjar for a third successive race as Max Verstappen's team-mate at Red Bull, while Yuki Tsunoda continues at Racing Bulls. Hadjar suffered a hairline fracture in a bone in his wrist during the summer break in a routine workout that involved boxing which forced him to miss the Dutch, Italian and now Spanish Grands Prix. messages.text: Leicester have sunk to new low under Martin but can he turn it around?

metadata.summary: A decade ago in September 2016, Leicester City were getting ready to play in the Champions League.
metadata.content: Leicester City sink to new low in League One but can Russell Martin turn it around? | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Leicester City sink to new low in League One but can Russell Martin turn it around? Leicester City find themselves sat 17th in League One after an embarrassing 4-0 home defeat against Oxford United on Saturday; Russell Martin is already under pressure after just one win in their first five games. Monday 7 September 2026 15:14, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Can Russell Martin turn Leicester's fortunes around after a poor start to the season in League One - here's what the EFL Show panel think. A decade ago in September 2016, Leicester City were getting ready to play in the Champions League. Now? They sit 17th in League One, the lowest position in the club's history since they entered the Football League in 1894. Russell Martin has led the Foxes to just one win in their first five games, and on Saturday they were battered 4-0 at home by Oxford United. Leicester fans were chanting 'you're getting sacked in the morning' at Martin at the King Power Stadium, who would have been desperate for a good start to turn his reputation around after a dismal end to his time at Southampton, and then a gruelling spell at Rangers. metadata.summary: Red Roses head coach John Mitchell has named an experienced 36-player squad for the home leg of the WXV Global Series, with 25 World Cup winners included.
metadata.content: Red Roses name 25 World Cup winners in 36-player squad for home leg of WXV Global Series | Rugby Union News | Sky Sports Skip to content Red Roses name 25 World Cup winners in 36-player squad for home leg of WXV Global Series England face Australia on Saturday 12 September, before meeting Canada in a repeat of their 2025 World Cup final clash a week later; they round off the home leg of the series against New Zealand at Allianz Stadium in front of over 50,000 spectators on Saturday 26 September Monday 7 September 2026 13:49, UK Image: World Cup winner Ellie Kildunne is part of the Red Roses squads announced for the home leg of the WXV Global Series Red Roses head coach John Mitchell has named an experienced 36-player squad for the home leg of the WXV Global Series, with 25 World Cup winners included. Led by captain Megan Jones, the squad contains a combined 1,234 international caps, while there are three as yet uncapped players picked in the form of Bryony Field, Hayley Jones and Sophie McQueen. England take on Australia at CorpAcq Stadium in the outskirts of Manchester on Saturday September 12, before meeting Canada in a repeat of their 2025 World Cup final clash at Sandy Park, Exeter, a week later.
